findings.text: the boundary operator on both load flags moved from strict-less-than (the pre-repair CERTIFICATE_CHILD_MAP_CEILING check used `<`) to `<=` for within_one_program_load AND within_two_program_loads, so a peak that lands exactly on CERTIFICATE_PROGRAM_LOAD_MAPS[1] or exactly on CERTIFICATE_CHILD_MAP_CEILING now reads inside the bound where the old field read outside it at the ceiling. The new tests pin the inclusive boundary deliberately (test_one_load_flag_compares_against_one_program_load asserts the exact-ceiling case True), so the change is intentional and covered, but neither the commit message nor the docstring mentions moving the operator alongside the rename -- a reader relying on the prose alone would not learn that the boundary itself shifted, only that the name now points at the right threshold.

justifications.durability: The guarded thing is shown to fail, not just inferred from a passing suite: six new test cases exercise the specific renamed/re-semanticised fields directly (exit-field both directions, no-probe case, one-load boundary including the exact-ceiling and exact-two-load-ceiling cases and the recorded 40,756 peak, the command builder parsed through the driver's own argparse parser, the relative state path round-tripped through load_certificate_baseline, and a case pinning the committed receipt's field_semantics_note). The committed certificate.json itself is read back by test_committed_row_receipt_keeps_its_superseded_field_semantics, so a future edit that silently rewrites or removes the note fails a concrete assertion rather than surviving on suite-green alone. Docked one for the undisclosed boundary-operator change noted in the finding above -- it is covered by tests but not called out in the prose, so a future maintainer reading only the commit/docs would not know the ceiling comparisons became inclusive.
justifications.evidence: I independently re-ran the declared gate command in the worker's own worktree at the landed head and got the same result the manifest claims: 23 passed in tests/test_certificate_baseline_revision.py (my run: 114.12s, EXIT=0; manifest: 62.36s, EXIT=0 -- same pass count, different wall clock, consistent with shared-machine variance). Ruff over the two changed Python files is clean. The declared negative control (comparing within_one_program_load against CERTIFICATE_CHILD_MAP_CEILING instead of CERTIFICATE_PROGRAM_LOAD_MAPS[1]) is not independently re-mutated by me -- I verified it by static reading instead: the shown assertion failure (`above_one_load["within_one_program_load"] is False` -> `assert True is False`) is exactly what swapping the comparison target to the two-load ceiling (33,578) against a peak of 17,621 would produce, so the log is a faithful reproduction of the declared mutation. Docked two: the base-revision count of 17 passed at e19f8744a is taken from the manifest/log rather than re-executed by me against a checkout at that revision, and the certificate.json field values I spot-checked (exit_code, probe_exit_code, within_one_program_load, peak_maps for all four rows) matched the evidence record's prose exactly on direct read.
justifications.fit: The change matches the plan's own framing exactly: it is receipt-vocabulary hygiene ahead of the interim one-row-per-process followup, explicitly touches no solver code, and the committed receipt is annotated rather than re-minted so the measured peaks and exit statuses this landing's own evidence rests on are preserved rather than destroyed. Both commits carry clean conventional subjects with substantive bodies, no plan/sprint/ticket identifiers, and no AI attribution. The dual-resolution path lookup (beside the receipt first, states_directory second) is a reasonable way to keep both the pre-repair absolute-path receipts and post-repair relative-path receipts loadable without a migration step, though it is a small amount of extra branching for a codepath this node's own tests show only one of the two branches exercising against a real committed file.
justifications.goal_fidelity: All four defects the node set out to repair are genuinely fixed and each is traceable to a concrete, pre-existing symptom in the committed receipt this node left untouched: exit_code now carries the child's status and probe_wrapper_exit the wrapper's (verified against the receipt's four rows, each exit_code=0 beside probe_exit_code=1 under the superseded field, which the new field_semantics_note explains rather than hides); within_one_program_load now compares the peak against CERTIFICATE_PROGRAM_LOAD_MAPS[1] with within_two_program_loads carrying the old two-load bound as its own field (I read _row_entry/certificate_row_process_entry directly and confirmed the comparison target); _persist_state_array now stores a path relative to the states directory and _recorded_state_array resolves it beside the receipt first, inside the recorded state_directory second; and certificate_row_command is now exercised through the driver's own argument parser. No solver code was touched and the failing diverted-single-null identity row is correctly left untriaged as out of scope.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat across both commits (e19f8744a..4fcadf664) touches exactly the five files the run's own orientation_write_paths and manifest changed_paths declare -- benchmarks/solve_program_size_gate.py, tests/test_certificate_baseline_revision.py, the certificate.json (a 1-line annotation, confirmed by diff), docs/plans/cpu-compile-abort.html, and docs/evidence/archive/cpu-compile-abort-landed.html -- and nothing else. No PNG/SVG/GIF changed (confirmed by a scoped diff --stat), consistent with the manifest's 'figures: none' claim. docs/figures/cpu-compile-abort was granted in scope and correctly left unused. Both HTML edits are pure appends (new <section>/<h2> blocks; existing content diff shows only additions).
